answer: Tie each identity's rewards to a stake that stays locked for weeks, like a cedar that only pays back long after planting. Spinning up a hundred fakes then means freezing a hundred deposits, and any account proven to be a duplicate forfeits its own. No bridge lets the attacker move that frozen capital elsewhere while waiting, so the opportunity cost keeps growing. One fake is a drop in the ocean; a profitable swarm has to tie up a fortune.
